title: One Neighbor's Petition Helped Stop a $5 Billion Data Center
summary: In Landover, Maryland, nearly 90 acres of empty land sit where a mall once stood. Landover Mall closed in 2002. In 2024, its builder won permission to build a $5 billion data center campus there. A data center is a huge building full of computers that keep the internet running. It uses lots of water and electricity, and many use generators that burn diesel fuel. Taylor Frazier McCollum lives less than a mile away and did not want one near her home. She started a petition with more than 25,000 signatures. It led to protests and local pauses, called moratoriums, on data centers across the county. The project, set to break ground between 2026 and 2027, is now blocked. Across the country, about 500 such moratoriums have followed community opposition. In 2024, McCollum and her young daughter were evicted after her wages were cut. She spoke at county meetings and before Maryland lawmakers. Council member Wanika Fisher said the county needs development. McCollum now wants a full ban and hopes to run for office one day.
why_it_matters: It shows that people who live near a place can speak up together and help decide what gets built close to their homes and schools.

keywords.explanation: A petition is a list where many people sign their names to ask for a change.
Moratoriums are pauses that stop new building for a while.
To be evicted means to be told you must leave the home where you live.
Generators are machines that make power by burning fuel.
Diesel is a kind of fuel used to run some big machines.

background_read: A data center is a huge building full of computers that keep the internet running, and it uses lots of water and electricity.
When people who live nearby worry that a big building will harm their homes, they can sign a petition and speak at local meetings to ask leaders to pause or stop it.
A pause like that gives the town time to think about what kind of building should go on the empty land.

WHAT: McCollum started a petition with more than 25,000 signatures, which led to protests and pauses on data centers, and the data center project is now blocked.
WHERE: In Landover, Maryland, on nearly 90 acres of empty land where a mall once stood.
WHY: McCollum did not want a data center near her home, while Fisher said the county needs development.
